entities.summary:
The Battle of Fort Sumter was a pivotal naval engagement that marked the opening salvo of the American Civil War. 

 On April 12, 1861, Confederate forces under General P.G.T. Beauregard bombarded Union-held Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina. The 34-hour bombardment, which ended on April 13, 1861, was the first military action of the Civil War and set in motion a chain of events that would divide the nation.

 The battle was a decisive Confederate victory, but its significance extends far beyond the immediate outcome. The war that followed would claim the lives of over 600,000 soldiers and civilians, redraw the nation's political map, and leave a lasting legacy of racial tension and social upheaval. 

 The echoes of Fort Sumter can be heard in the ongoing struggles for civil rights and racial justice that continue to shape American society today.
